heroHeadline: Huawei Captures ~60% of China's AI Chip Market; US Extends Equipment Controls to Hua Hong as Semiconductor War Enters New Phase
heroSubtitle: Huawei is on track to command approximately 60% of China's domestic AI accelerator chip market in 2026 — exceeding earlier 50% projections — as Nvidia's effective exit from China's leading-edge AI segment creates structural domestic dominance; Huawei AI chip revenues are forecast at $12 billion (+60% YoY), with an upgraded Ascend 950DT planned for Q4 2026. On April 29, the US Department of Commerce escalated by ordering Lam Research, Applied Materials, and KLA to halt chipmaking equipment shipments to Hua Hong Semiconductor (China's #2 chipmaker) — the first expansion of equipment controls beyond SMIC, targeting Hua Hong's 7nm development programs in Wuxi and Shanghai. Chinese Premier Li Qiang on May 1 declared that China-made AI models have 'spearheaded the global open-source AI ecosystem' — the most senior official endorsement of Beijing's strategy to use open-source AI distribution as a geopolitical tool against US AI leadership, as DeepSeek V4's MIT-licensed release continues to drive global adoption. The structural dynamic of the China tech war has now crossed a threshold: Huawei's 60% domestic AI chip dominance, ByteDance's $5.6B Ascend commitment, DeepSeek V4's Huawei-native optimization, and China's NDRC veto of Meta's Manus AI acquisition together confirm that every dimension of the US-China AI decoupling — compute, models, capital flows, and corporate ownership — is now structurally separated. The Hua Hong action may paradoxically accelerate specialty chip self-sufficiency in sectors (automotive, power management) that had been less pressured to localize.
